segments.title: Welcome
segments.script: Welcome to Working with AI at Alder. In the next fifteen minutes, we'll cover what generative AI is, where it fits in your work, and the rules that keep our customers' information safe.

segments.title: What generative AI is
segments.verified: No checkable policy claims; wording still consistent with policy v3.0
segments.script: Generative AI tools produce text, images, and code from a prompt. They're fast, they're confident, and they're sometimes wrong. That's why our policy is about judgment as much as it is about tools.

segments.title: Approved tools
segments.script: Right now, generative AI tools like ChatGPT are not approved for business use at Alder. Don't use them for work tasks, even on a personal device.

segments.title: Customer data
segments.script: Never enter customer or policyholder information into any AI tool. That includes names, policy numbers, claim details, and anything from a customer file.

segments.title: Judgment
segments.script: AI output is a draft, not a decision. Check the facts, check the tone, and check that nothing confidential slipped in before anything leaves your hands.

segments.title: Customer communications
segments.script: If you use AI to help draft an email or letter to a customer, you don't need to disclose it, but you are responsible for every word.

segments.title: When you're not sure
segments.script: If you're not sure whether a use is allowed, ask before you act. Questions go to the AI Council through the Ask AI Council channel in Slack.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.script: That's the policy in fifteen minutes. Protect customer information, use your judgment, and ask when you're not sure. Next up, a short knowledge check.

publish.how: New audio track muxed into the video under the same media ID, captions regenerated from word timing. Every embed of the video updates at once.

segments.title: Start from the claim
segments.script: In this walkthrough, you'll settle a total-loss auto claim in ClaimsCore, from valuation to payment. Start from the claim file.

segments.title: Open the worksheet
segments.script: From the left navigation, open the Payments tab. The settlement worksheet opens, with the vehicle valuation on the right.

segments.title: Confirm the numbers
segments.script: Confirm the actual cash value, then apply the deductible and any lienholder payoff. The net amount updates as you go.

segments.title: Route for approval
segments.script: If the settlement needs a supervisor's approval, select Hold for Review. The claim waits in the queue until your supervisor signs off.

segments.title: Salvage and title
segments.script: Review the salvage and title steps before you issue payment. Each step has to be acknowledged, or the payment button stays gray.

segments.title: Issue payment
segments.script: Once approved, the payment posts to the claim, and the customer receives a settlement letter automatically. That completes the walkthrough.

segments.title: Welcome
segments.script: Welcome to Alder Mutual. This course walks you through your first ninety days: who we are, how we work, what we offer you, and where to go for help.

segments.title: How we work
segments.script: Alder is remote-first. Most teams gather in the Austin or Dallas office two days a week, on anchor days your manager sets.

segments.title: How we're led
segments.script: Alder is led by chief executive Elena Marsh and a leadership team that started out in claims, underwriting, and the field.

segments.title: Benefits enrollment
segments.script: Your benefits enrollment window opens on your first day and closes after thirty days. The benefits team hosts drop-in sessions every Tuesday.

segments.title: Leave and savings
segments.script: Parents get twelve weeks of paid parental leave, and Alder matches your 401(k) contributions up to four percent.
segments.tts: Parents get twelve weeks of paid parental leave, and Alder matches your four oh one K contributions up to four percent.

segments.title: Travel and expenses
segments.script: Book travel and file expenses in Concur. Receipts are required for anything over seventy-five dollars.

segments.title: Day ninety
segments.script: By day ninety, you'll have finished your required training, met your team, and set your first goals with your manager. Welcome aboard.

publish.how: Rise block audio replaced, course republished, uploaded as a new version of the same LMS course. Because the change is material, assigned learners are notified.

segments.title: Why speak up
segments.script: Speaking up is how we protect each other and the people we insure. This lesson covers what to report, how to report it, and what happens next.

segments.title: How to report
segments.script: You can report a concern to your manager, to People Operations, or anonymously through the Speak Up line at 1-800-555-0142, twenty-four hours a day.
segments.tts: You can report a concern to your manager, to People Operations, or anonymously through the Speak Up line at one, eight hundred, five five five, zero one four two, twenty-four hours a day.

segments.title: What happens next
segments.script: Every report is reviewed by Ethics & Compliance within two business days. You'll get a case number, and you can check its status anonymously.

segments.title: No retaliation
segments.script: Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is a violation of policy, full stop.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.script: If something feels wrong, say something. That's the whole lesson.

segments.title: Path introduction
segments.script: Before your first sale, complete three foundations: Security Basics 2023, Insurance Fundamentals, and HomeShield Plus product training. HomeShield Plus is our flagship homeowners policy, with water backup available as an add-on.

segments.title: The six weeks ahead
segments.script: Over six weeks you'll shadow a senior agent, quote your first policies in the sandbox, and sit for your certification.
